title_zh: 前《时代》杂志记者、副国务卿斯特罗布·塔尔博特去世
meta_line: 来源：NPR · World ｜ 难度：B2 ｜ 词数：369
summary: 这是一篇 NPR 的讣告报道，讲述美国外交官、前《时代》杂志记者斯特罗布·塔尔博特的一生。文章从他与克林顿在牛津同住的青年时代写起，重点讲述他因协助翻译赫鲁晓夫回忆录而成名并进入《时代》，此后又应克林顿之邀进入国务院、主导对俄政策。随后回顾他执掌布鲁金斯学会、主持外交政策委员会、著书十余部的经历。全文语言平实，但使用了不少新闻报道里常见、学习者却拿不准的动词与惯用表达。

vocab.example_zh: 斯特罗布·塔尔博特曾是一名《时代》杂志记者，后在比尔·克林顿总统任内担任副国务卿，之后又执掌布鲁金斯学会，他于周四逝世。

grammar.sentence: Strobe Talbott, a former Time magazine reporter who later served as deputy secretary of state under President Bill Clinton and then headed the Brookings Institution, died Thursday.
grammar.point: 长同位语 + 定语从句（主语与谓语被隔开）
grammar.explain_zh: 主语 Strobe Talbott 后面插入了一个同位语 a former Time magazine reporter，同位语里又套了一个 who 引导的定语从句，把“记者—副国务卿—布鲁金斯学会会长”三段履历一次说清，谓语 died Thursday 直到句尾才出现。这是英文讣告和新闻导语的典型写法：名字先行，身份层层展开，最后才给出“死亡”这个核心事件，形成“人名—履历—结局”的信息节奏，也避免了拆成好几个短句。

grammar.sentence: While at the British university, after interning for Time in Moscow, the magazine asked Talbott to help translate the leaked memoirs of Nikita Khrushchev, the former first secretary of the Communist Party of the Soviet Union who was ousted in 1964.
grammar.point: 状语从句的省略 + 多重状语前置 + 句末同位语
grammar.explain_zh: While at the British university 是省略形式，完整应为 While he was at the British university（当从句主语与主句主语一致且含 be 动词时可省略主语和 be）。后面 after interning for Time in Moscow 又是一个介词短语状语，两个时间状语叠加，先把时间脉络交代清楚。宾语后面又接了同位语 the former first secretary...，并再次套上 who 引导的定语从句解释赫鲁晓夫的身份。把长修饰成分放在句末，符合英语的“尾重原则”（end weight），句子读起来更稳。

grammar.sentence: "Strobe was a good and brilliant man who made our world more peaceful and secure," said Clinton in a statement after Talbott's death.
grammar.point: 引语前置 + 主谓倒装（said Clinton）
grammar.explain_zh: 直接引语放在最前面，后面用 said Clinton 而不是 Clinton said，构成主谓倒装。这种“引语 + 动词 + 说话人”的结构在新闻报道中非常常见：读者的注意力先落在引语内容上，再从后半句得到消息来源。注意倒装后仍用名词 Clinton，如果说话人用代词则一般不到装（如 he said），这是英文引语呈现的一条小规律。

questions.q: Which of the following best captures the main purpose of the article?
questions.a: 报道斯特罗布·塔尔博特去世的消息，并回顾他作为记者、副国务卿和智库负责人的一生主要经历。文章以讣告的方式按时间线串起他的学业、新闻生涯、外交生涯、智库工作与著述，重点是“介绍逝者的身份与贡献”，而不是评论某项政策或表达作者个人态度。

questions.q: What can be inferred about the relationship between Talbott and Clinton from the article?
questions.a: 两人的关系远不止普通的上下级。留学牛津时他们同住一室，塔尔博特翻译赫鲁晓夫回忆录时克林顿还每天给他做早饭；多年后克林顿当选总统，又主动打电话邀请塔尔博特进入国务院。可见这是一段从青年时代延续到政治生涯的私人友谊，并且这种友谊影响了塔尔博特的职业轨迹。

questions.q: Why does the article bring up Talbott's translation of Khrushchev's memoirs?
questions.a:
因为这件事在他的人生中起到了关键作用：一方面它让年轻的塔尔博特一举成名，并为他换来《时代》杂志的工作，成为他新闻生涯的起点；另一方面，这本回忆录涉及苏联高层政治，也解释了他后来为何长期专注苏美关系。文章提到它，是为了交代他专业兴趣和职业道路的起点，同时呼应他与克林顿在牛津时期的那段交情。

article: Strobe Talbott, a former Time magazine reporter who later served as deputy secretary of state under President Bill Clinton and then headed the Brookings Institution, died Thursday. He was 80.
His son, Devin Talbott, confirmed he passed away peacefully after a long illness in his East Hampton, New York, home.

The elder Talbott was educated at Yale and Oxford, where he bunked with Clinton. While at the British university, after interning for Time in Moscow, the magazine asked Talbott to help translate the leaked memoirs of Nikita Khrushchev, the former first secretary of the Communist Party of the Soviet Union who was ousted in 1964.
Talbott did, and it gave him some notoriety as a young man and a job at the magazine.

After 21 years at Time, where he focused on Soviet-American relations and held positions including Washington bureau chief and a foreign-affairs columnist, according to his U.S. State Department biography, he received a call from the newly elected Clinton.

Talbott joined the U.S. State Department in 1994, swiftly becoming deputy secretary of state. In that role, he was the architect of the Clinton administration's approach to Russia and other formerly Soviet countries and conducted negotiations between the U.S. and India after the latter's nuclear tests in 1998.

"Strobe was a good and brilliant man who made our world more peaceful and secure," said Clinton in a statement after Talbott's death. When Talbott was translating Khrushchev's memoirs while at Oxford, it was Clinton's job to make him breakfast every day, he said, adding, "somehow, I got the better end of the deal."
Both he and Hillary were "deeply saddened" by the passing of "a wonderful friend, and a world-class human being," he said.
Afterward, he served as the president of Brookings from 2002 to 2017. In that time, he also chaired the U.S. State Department's Foreign Affairs Policy Board.
Talbott also authored over a dozen books. His last book was titled "Our Founders' Warning: The Age of Reason Meets the Age of Trump," which was published in 2020.
He was born in Dayton, Ohio, in 1946, and is survived by two sons, Devin and Adrian, and six grandchildren.
His first wife, Brook Shearer, died in 2009, and he later married author Barbara Lazear Ascher.
